correctness.rationale: The cited smooth-curve formulas and adjunction give deg Tan=D(S-N+1) and deg Sec=D(D-S+N-2)/2. Their comparison is equivalent to product(y_i+1)<=3 sum y_i+1. The coordinate increment of the difference is product over the other factors minus three, yielding the stated exclusion for four or more defining equations and the three remaining triples in codimension three. Fresh exact enumeration of 75,504 bounded tuples reproduced exactly those cases and the degree pairs, while the proof is uniform and does not rely on the enumeration.

final_claim: For smooth complete-intersection curves in projective dimension at least four with all defining degrees at least two, the secant degree is at most the tangent degree exactly for (2,2,2), (2,2,3), and (2,2,4) in projective four-space, with equality only for (2,2,4).
